ftp_curve_construction.text: `funds_transfer_pricing_ftp` answers "how is one deal's spread split up?": from `notional`, `customer_rate`, `ftp_rate` and an optional `liquidity_premium`, it adds the premium to `ftp_rate` to get an all-in transfer rate, then measures the lending margin against that all-in rate. `is_asset` reverses the sign for a deposit. `ftp_curve_construction` answers "what transfer rate belongs at each maturity?": it takes `tenors`, `base_curve` and `liquidity_spreads` and adds the spread to the base rate at each tenor. The curve can feed the deal function's `ftp_rate`. Because the curve already contains a liquidity spread, also setting `liquidity_premium` could count liquidity twice, so use one or the other deliberately.

explain.text: `funds_transfer_pricing_ftp` (Funds Transfer Pricing FTP) breaks a single deal into margin components, given its `notional`, `customer_rate` and matched-maturity `ftp_rate`. A `liquidity_premium` can be added on top of the FTP rate. For an asset (a loan, the default via `is_asset`), the lending unit's commercial margin is the customer rate less the all-in FTP rate, applied to the notional. For a liability (a deposit), the margin is the all-in FTP rate less the customer rate. It also returns the total spread, which is the absolute gap between the two rates times the notional.

when.text:
`funds_transfer_pricing_ftp` (Funds Transfer Pricing FTP) fits when you want to break a single deal's pricing into margin components:

- You have one loan (asset) or one deposit (liability) and want to see how its spread splits between the business unit and central treasury.
- You already have a matched-maturity transfer rate for the deal (`ftp_rate`) and want to apply it to the customer rate (`customer_rate`) on a given `notional`.
- You need a liquidity charge added to the transfer rate, using `liquidity_premium`, before judging the deal's commercial margin.
- You want to compare an asset and a liability on the same footing by switching `is_asset`.

- Building the transfer curve itself: `ftp_curve_construction` is listed as constructing a matched-maturity FTP curve, a base curve plus a liquidity spread.
